{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that personal moral standards (PMS) would show positive correlations with moral values, virtues, and judgments, and that concern over moral mistakes (CMM) would show distinct relationships with these variables, specifically predicting that CMM would show a unique positive correlation with indebtedness after controlling for PMS.",
  "design": "correlational",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Personal moral standards (PMS) and concern over moral mistakes (CMM) as measured by an adapted version of the Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale.",
  "outcome_measure": "Indebtedness, measured as part of a gratitude judgment task involving a vignette about receiving help.",
  "population_and_setting": "539 university students in the eastern coastal region of the People's Republic of China.",
  "sample_size_total": 539,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited after classes; no compensation provided.",
  "analysis_plan": "Partial correlations between moral perfectionism dimensions (PMS and CMM) and moral outcomes (including indebtedness), controlling for the overlap between PMS and CMM.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used three separate samples (N=168, N=206, N=165) to measure different moral outcomes. The focal effect pertains to the partial correlation analysis conducted across the samples to isolate the unique variance of the two perfectionism dimensions."
}
